newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end mixed after setting new highs.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end mixed after setting new highs.

text.p: CME live cattle futures closed mostly lower on profit taking after setting new contract highs in October and December early following strong cash markets.
October set a new contract high of 72.450 cents per lb and December 68.750 cents before slipping on the profit taking. Futures closed 0.325 higher to 0.225 lower with October up most at 72.325 cents.
Futures set new highs early following reports that some fed cattle traded up $1 at $71 per cwt. Commercial demand pushed futures up to new highs before the profit taking developed, they said.
Boxed beef values have continued to rise and packers' cattle supplies appear to be tight enough to prompt increased interest for fed cattle. Feedlots were asking $72, they added.
Heavyweight choice boxed beef rose to $104.40 per cwt Monday, the highest level since August 22, and fed cattle prices recently reached highest price levels since April 1995.
Back months also showed seasonal resistance which kept them at a discount despite late fund rolling, buying of December and selling of October, commonly known as the "Goldman roll".
They will see more cattle into the winter, they said.
"You are getting into winter and you usually do see a few more cattle," said Dave Maher, analyst for Securities Corp of Iowa, referring to the weakness in deferred cattle futures.
R.J. O'Brien bought October late while Refco sold on the spread, pit sources said.
In live cattle options, there was commercial hedging in back months. Refco bought February 64 puts and sold 68 calls and also bought December 67 puts and sold 70 calls, pit sources added.
Feeder cattle futures were pressured by higher grain futures, traders said.

Concern over rising feed costs prompted scattered profit taking. Trade was also nervous ahead of Wednesday's USDA grain production report which offset underlying support from the rising CME feeder cattle index, they said.
The latest CME index was up $0.66 at $64.04 per cwt, the highest level since December 27.
Smith Barney sold at the close. Cargill Investor Services and Iowa Grain bought late and LFG sold, pit sources said.
Feeder cattle closed 0.425 to 0.050 cent lower with October off 0.375 at 63.875 cents a lb.
